CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to reassess treatment efficacy for generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches. Focus on evaluating symptom control, medication adjustments, and overall quality of life since the last visit.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, reporting a mixed response to the current treatment regimen. He expresses that his anxiety remains stable, but he continues to struggle with irritability, particularly in high-pressure situations at work. While he has adhered to his sertraline regimen of 300 mg daily, he notes persistent difficulty with concentration and memory recall, which he finds increasingly debilitating during his work tasks.
Mr. Smith reports a slight increase in the frequency of his tension-type headaches, now occurring approximately twice a week, with an intensity ranging from 4 to 6 out of 10. He continues to take topiramate at 150 mg daily, which he believes helps manage the pain, but he has increased his ibuprofen usage to twice a month due to the heightened headache frequency. Sleep quality remains satisfactory, averaging 7 to 8 hours per night, aided by trazodone and melatonin. However, he continues to experience significant morning grogginess, which he describes as a barrier to starting his day effectively.
Despite the improvements in sleep, Mr. Smith reports that his afternoon fatigue has worsened, attributing it to increased work demands and stressors. He expresses a desire to explore additional strategies to combat this fatigue, as it is severely impacting his productivity and overall well-being.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 300 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 75 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 4. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (increased frequency) 5. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (continued) 6. Topiramate 150 mg daily (continued) 7. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (continued) 8. Melatonin 3 mg at bedtime (continued) 9. Gabapentin 200 mg at bedtime (discontinued)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to engage in regular physical exercise, including brisk walking and hiking on weekends. He has maintained a reduced caffeine intake and adheres to a balanced diet, which he feels has been beneficial for his anxiety management. His mindfulness practices, including meditation and yoga, are still integral to his daily routine, and he continues to journal for emotional processing. However, he reports that work-related stress has begun to encroach upon his ability to maintain these healthy habits.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Anxiety levels stable; persistent irritability noted; sleep quality satisfactory; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms. - Neurological: Increased headache frequency; no dizziness or visual disturbances reported. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Worsening fatigue reported, particularly in the afternoons, with no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 120/75 mmHg, HR 70 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented; appears moderately fatigued but engaged; mood appears anxious with mild distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed; no tenderness in the temporal region. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears anxious with mild distress.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 300 mg daily. Recommend ongoing cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) to further address irritability and concentration issues. Consider discussing potential adjustments to the medication regimen, including the option of increasing the dose of sertraline if symptoms persist. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 75 mg at bedtime and melatonin 3 mg nightly; assess efficacy and side effects in one month. Monitor for any changes in sleep architecture. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue topiramate at 150 mg daily; maintain headache diary to monitor frequency and intensity. Consider referral to a neurologist if headache patterns worsen or new symptoms develop. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Discuss the introduction of modafinil to address fatigue, pending evaluation of sleep quality and potential underlying conditions. Referral to a sleep specialist is recommended for further evaluation of possible sleep apnea or thyroid dysfunction. Reinforce the importance of stress management techniques and lifestyle modifications to enhance energy levels.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-06-20 to evaluate symptom progression, medication efficacy, and discuss any new concerns. Mr. Smith is encouraged to maintain open communication regarding his treatment response and any lifestyle changes he implements.
